tags.qa_note: RE-AUDITED 2026-09-18 (6 independent sources). Built 1954 (Navalmeccanica shipyard, Castellammare di Stabia, Naples, Italy per Atlantic Cable historical archive) as CS Salernum; sold 1984 to Transoceanic Cableship Co. (AT&T subsidiary) and renamed Charles L. Brown — build year and rename corroborated by atlantic-cable.com, DAN, and Divertrek. Purchased by Statia for $1 in 2002; deliberately scuttled July 25, 2003 (date corroborated independently by DAN Alert Diver and Scuba Diving magazine/Caribbean Compass). LENGTH CONFLICTS ACROSS SOURCES: Golden Rock says 300ft; DAN, Caribbean Compass and Scuba Diving magazine say 320ft; Divertrek and Scubaqua say 327ft/100m; the vessel's original 1954 registry (Atlantic Cable archive) lists 339.6ft — sources report length between roughly 300 and 340 feet (91-104m). Gross tonnage (2,789 GT) appears in only ONE source (Atlantic Cable archive) and is NOT independently corroborated, so omitted from markdown per 2-source rule. Sinking cause: no accidental cause is corroborated — the ship was deliberately flooded/scuttled to create the reef; Scuba Diving magazine reports it took 1-2 hours to go under, consistent with a controlled flooding (one single-sourced Divertrek claim of a 'burst pipe' equipment failure could not be corroborated and was omitted). Lies on STARBOARD side per DAN, Divertrek, Scubaqua. MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: previous markdown listed groupers, moray eels, lionfish, snapper/grunt schools, stingrays, and hawksbill turtles — NONE of these are confirmed by current dive-shop sources for this specific wreck. Confirmed site-specific species (Golden Rock + Scubaqua + DiverTrek + DAN): Caribbean reef sharks, cubera snapper, a resident barracuda nicknamed 'Charlie' (confirmed independently by both Golden Rock and DAN), horse-eye jacks, yellow-headed jawfish, angelfish, sea turtles (species unspecified), spotted eagle rays. Markdown marine life section rewritten accordingly.

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-18. Anchor Point confirmed on leeward coast with 18th-century French anchor c.1750-1775 (over 3m long, over 1 ton) per Divertrek; DAN's separate 'A Salute to St. Eustatius' article independently confirms a large anchor embedded in the reef. Depth ~18m/60ft confirmed by Scubaqua. MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: previous markdown listed groupers, yellowtail snapper, blue tang, French angelfish, southern stingrays, garden eels, hawksbill turtles — none of these are confirmed by current site-specific sources. Confirmed: moray eels, Caribbean reef sharks, Spanish hogfish, drumfish, sharptail eels, lobsters (Scubaqua), hawksbill turtles (DAN, corroborating one prior claim). Markdown marine life section rewritten accordingly.

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-18. DEPTH BUG FIXED: field was still 10m despite the 2026-06-29 qa_note already stating '~55ft/17m confirmed' — corrected to 17m (Scubaqua and Divertrek both give ~55ft/17m). Beads are Dutch/Amsterdam-made cobalt-blue glass trade beads, confirmed by lifeonthegoldenrock.wordpress.com ('made in Amsterdam, out of glass') and DAN ('Dutch blue beads, historical currency'). ORIGIN THEORY CONFLICT: lifeonthegoldenrock.wordpress.com itself presents TWO competing, unconfirmed theories for how beads concentrated at this spot — (1) a bead-laden ship sank there, or (2) freed slaves threw beads into the sea after emancipation and they drifted to this spot — and does not assert either as fact. Divertrek separately floats a shipwreck-at-Crook's-reef origin. Markdown corrected to present both theories as unresolved speculation rather than asserting the emancipation story as settled history. DROPPED wearestatia.com as a source — it incorrectly describes the beads as 'currency used by indigenous people,' which contradicts every other source (beads were Dutch-made and used in Atlantic slave-trade commerce); its 'vertical swim-through called The Abyss' claim is also uncorroborated and removed from markdown. MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: previous markdown listed blue tang, parrotfish, sergeant majors, garden eels, flounder, green sea turtles — none confirmed for this specific site. Confirmed: flying gurnards (Scubaqua AND DAN, independently), pike blennies, sailfin blennies, scorpionfish, mantis shrimp (Scubaqua).

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-18 (4 independent sources). Golden Rock, Scubaqua, and MyScubaDivingGearGuide all independently confirm this as a modern artificial reef — a sunken tugboat, barge, and ship hull/tanker sections — at approximately 18-20m. DAN's 'A Salute to St. Eustatius' article independently corroborates the multi-structure description ('harbor boat, tugboat, tanker sections'). MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: previous markdown added 'resident populations of groupers and moray eels in the hull structures' — not confirmed by any source, removed. Confirmed: large schools of reef fish, angelfish, garden eels, Caribbean/southern stingrays, pipe fish (Golden Rock); octopus, juvenile fish, yellow sponges, orange cup coral (Scubaqua); barracuda, lobsters (DAN).

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-18. SOURCE CORRECTION: scubaverse.com was cited previously but on direct re-check it does NOT mention Hangover at all — replaced with scubaqua.com, which does. Golden Rock confirms: coral-encrusted lava flow, 10-15m/30-45ft range, maze of lava flows with overhangs; type kept as wall (closest available enum value for overhang/ledge terrain — operators classify it separately from their formal 'Wall Dive' sites like Drop Off East, so this is a judgment call, not a confirmed 'wall' per operator taxonomy). MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: previous markdown listed copper sweepers, glassfish, bar jacks, horse-eye jacks, banded coral shrimp, green moray eels — none confirmed for this site. Confirmed: Caribbean reef sharks, hawksbill turtles (DAN), rays, queen conch, spiny lobster (Golden Rock); yellow-head jawfish, peacock flounder, spotted drumfish, moray eels, angelfish (four species per Scubaqua), yellow-tail damselfish (Scubaqua); snapper (DAN).

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-18. SOURCE CORRECTION: goldenrockdive.com, divertrek.com and wearestatia.com were cited previously, but on direct re-check none of the three currently mention Crooks Castle by name (Golden Rock's live dive-sites page lists only 9 sites and Crooks Castle is not among them; wearestatia.com and divertrek.com do not mention it either). Re-verified instead via PADI's dive-site directory (contributed by Golden Rock, coordinates match ours: boat access, buoy #21, beginner, max depth 32.8ft/10m), Zentacle (same depth/access/difficulty), and STENAPA's own park page (statiapark.org), which names Crooks Castle as a boat-accessible beginner site/snorkel spot near a historic fort with 'always a sea turtle or stingray hanging around.' Depth (10m) and difficulty (Beginner) reconfirmed. MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: previous markdown listed French/queen angelfish, spotted drums, yellowhead jawfish, cleaning stations, reef squid, frogfish — none confirmed by current sources. Confirmed: sea turtle, stingray (PADI/Zentacle/statiapark.org consistently).

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-18 (4 independent sources). Golden Rock confirms: archaeological site, 18m/60ft depth, beginner level, ~2 min boat ride. Remains of two 18th-century wooden merchant ships (hulls gone, anchors/ballast/cannon remain) reconfirmed by Scubaqua, Divertrek and MyScubaDivingGearGuide (all independently call it a c.300-year-old shipwreck site with ballast stones/anchors, ~18m). VESSEL IDENTITIES STILL UNRESOLVED: Scubaverse names the two vessels as 'Charles Brown' and 'Berkeley Springs,' 18th-century British naval ships — re-searched 2026-09-18 and STILL cannot find independent corroboration; every other reference to this claim traces back to the same Scubaverse-derived text, not a second independent source, and having a wreck named identically to the island's separate famous 'Charles Brown' wreck is itself suspicious. Vessel names remain OMITTED from markdown per 2-source rule. MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: previous markdown listed French/grey angelfish and moray eels (not confirmed) and called turtles 'hawksbill' (sources specify green, not hawksbill). Confirmed: southern stingrays (Golden Rock, Scubaqua, Divertrek — 3-way agreement), green turtles/sea turtles (Golden Rock, Scubaqua, Divertrek), reef fish, lobsters (Divertrek), blennies, cleaner shrimp, seahorses, frogfish (Scubaqua).

RE-AUDITED 2026-09-18. SOURCE CORRECTION: scubaverse.com was cited previously but on direct re-check it does NOT mention Nursing Station — replaced with padi.com, whose listed coordinates (17.46923,-62.99140) match ours almost exactly and which independently classifies the site as 'coral-encrusted lava flow.' Golden Rock confirms: 19m/63ft, beginner-intermediate, nurse sharks resting under overhangs. DAN's separate 'A Salute to St. Eustatius' article independently corroborates nurse sharks sleeping here and adds squirrelfish schools. MARINE LIFE CORRECTED: previous markdown also listed French/grey angelfish, Caribbean spiny lobster, bar jacks, and hawksbill turtles as if site-specific — none of these are confirmed by any source found this round; removed and replaced with the anti-hallucination caveat already used for shark counts, now extended to cover the rest of the list. Confirmed for this site: nurse sharks, lettuce sea slugs (Golden Rock); squirrelfish (DAN). Kept as Intermediate (not Beginner) due to topography and potential current, consistent with prior QA.
